feature: A copied Size measurement is named for what it measures
summary: Copying a Size measurement (Option drag, duplicate, or copy and paste) now names the copy for its size, "Size 274 × 62", instead of "Size 274 × 62 copy", so resizing the copy renames it to its new size. A copied Gap or Distance caliper keeps following its reading the same way.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/size-steps-and-resizes-walk.json.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press I, pick Size and click a button to measure it.
Press V, then Option-Command drag the measurement's box down to copy it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the copy's row in Layers: it says the same size as the original, with no "copy" on the end.
Drag the copy's bottom right corner handle to a new size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read Layers and Measurements: both say the new size, and the original still says its own.
Press Command-Z once: the copy's size and its name go back together.

evaluate: Is two rows both reading "Size 274 × 62" right after a copy clear enough, or would you rather the copy said it is a copy until it is changed?
Does a renamed copy (one you typed a name for) still reading "Save button copy" match what you expect?
Does pasting a measurement with Command-V name it the same way as Option dragging it?
rough: Two measurements of the same size share a name until one changes, exactly as two fresh measurements of the same thing always have; measurements are never numbered apart.

In the resized picture the copy's width chip is not on screen: the copy's bottom edge sits about 20 px above the canvas's bottom, and its chip lands below the canvas. Not part of this change; left in this task's log.
